comments.body: 2026-11-07 re-triage: do this before a_2vgzMmJ4x. vt-1.0.0 renames the dylib's install name to @rpath/libghostty-vt.1.dylib, and five places use the old name (dev:783, dev:902/1098/1125, install.rs:143, remote.rs:612). The gate stays green while --bundle fails, and no tier runs a remote Mac install. Linking statically deletes all of that, so it removes a risk from the move, and it lands and proves itself on the current pin. Note: the 1.0 ABI promise is no reason to keep a shared library, since Muster carries patches and builds its own.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description: Found by slot 1 in MIP-3 round 1 (a_2XJ1fr2cu fixes). The MIP assumed a static libghostty-vt collides with GhosttyKit in the app process (docs/observations/libghostty-9f9b8d1d.md section 8). It does not: libmuster.dylib is a cdylib exporting only include/muster.h's three symbols, so a static libghostty-vt inside it is invisible (verified: no ghostty or ubsan symbols exported, depends only on libSystem and libiconv). The 35 duplicate symbols in section 8 need both archives in one image. So the MUSTER_VT_LINK=static switch exists only to keep the app on a dylib it no longer needs. Linking statically everywhere would delete the env var and its rule, the dylib, both rpaths (.cargo/config.toml, Package.swift), and the bundle's Frameworks/libghostty-vt.dylib, at the cost of a copy of the library in libmuster and in the bridge. Worth doing as part of MIP-3's zero-debt goal; it touches bundle and release plumbing the gate does not exercise, so it needs ./dev --bundle and --contract to prove it. Probably alongside the distribution card (a_2XJ1ie3Ep).
title: Link libghostty-vt statically everywhere, and delete the dylib plumbing
